common_prompt:
SANCTUSARS FIXED PICTORIAL LANGUAGE. Create ONE new contemporary sacred fine-art painting, portrait 4:5. This is a complete painting, without typography, borders, logos or a space reserved for words. The attached images are the approved pictorial standard, not optional inspiration. Image 1 controls material, surface hierarchy and bold planes. Image 2 controls selective perception and the relationship of the viewer to the subject. Transfer that language to the NEW scriptural scene above. Do not copy angels, wings, swords, fig leaves or any other reference subject unless the new scene explicitly needs them.

PAINT THE SPACE BEFORE THE DETAILS. Establish two or three large, asymmetrical, interlocking color masses. Allow a substantial continuous area to remain quiet, translucent and spatially ambiguous: a plane can begin as architecture or cloth and lose its boundary into air. This is active pictorial space, not a large realistically rendered empty wall. Do not describe a complete room, street or landscape. Interrupt peripheral contours; omit incidental objects. Preserve just enough spatial clues for the stated encounter to be understood.

SURFACE HIERARCHY IS ESSENTIAL. The principal face, hand or gesture is exquisitely observed with thin luminous oil glazing and natural anatomy. Broad fields and most clothing are smooth or transparently washed, with very few internal marks. Reserve coarse pigment for one or two peripheral seams. Delicate watercolor-like optical layering may meet a sharp scraped paint edge. Never cover skin, cloth, air and stone with the same little strokes. A photographic scene with a texture filter is not this style.

Use a restrained family of mineral colors from the references with warm living skin as a small counterpoint. Avoid an all-beige scene, muddy sage-and-peach mixtures, antique sepia and the automatic blue-and-gold sunset. Mystery comes from incomplete space, the viewer's position, concealment and reflected light, not fantasy beams or generic heavenly clouds. Skin stays intact and alive. Eyes are softly readable; no hollow sockets, blue corpse faces or artificial doll smiles. Retain the biblical facts but omit explanatory scenery. No collage, comic panels, pencil, storybook rendering, aged varnish, all-over impasto or repeated mosaic brushwork. The fixed pictorial language governs style even if a scene description suggests otherwise.

A.direction: A / WIDE, SPATIAL ENCOUNTER. Make the figures relatively small and subordinate to an asymmetrical architecture of light and color, as in reference 1. The eye must travel through at least one concealed or incomplete plane before reaching the key encounter. Use depth and placement to express the scriptural relationship, not a line-up of figures along a blank wall. The biggest quiet field has changing translucency and interrupted boundaries rather than literal masonry. Keep any fully resolved face or hand small and precious. Favor cool pearl-white and a deep mineral dark, with one restrained color accent. Choose the actual arrangement from the scene; do not replicate the reference's diagonals or characters.

B.direction: B / INTIMATE, SELECTIVE DETAIL. Let one scripturally meaningful gesture, contact, gaze or object dominate an audacious crop. Resolve only that focal passage to intimate anatomical or material precision. Most surrounding cloth, shadow and architecture coalesce into broad quiet chromatic planes, as in reference 1. Let a few contours disappear without damaging living skin. Avoid multiple complete portraits, a collage of separate actions, or filling the picture with equally detailed folds. Use a deep mineral field with a pale luminous passage and localized skin warmth. The scene may feature hands, eyes or another meaningful detail; do not automatically repeat the reference's outstretched hands.

C.direction: C / UNUSUAL, MEANINGFUL PERCEPTION. Place the viewer in a position suggested by the scriptural relationship: partially concealed, looking obliquely from above or below, seeing a trace or a reflection rather than the entire action. Choose the device that fits this scene; a pond or an overhead shot is not mandatory. Borrow incomplete perception from reference 2 and the calm, expansive surface hierarchy from reference 1. Keep one tender living detail readable within a space that does not fully explain its geometry. A lower or higher camera angle in an otherwise fully described room is insufficient. Avoid giant foreground knees, a hand reaching at the lens by default, optical distortion or ominous faces. Use luminous near-white against a restrained blue-green or ink-dark field, never a sepia photographic interior.
